examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{窓|まど}の{外|そと}を{見|み}ている。
examples.english: The cat is looking outside the window.

examples.japanese: {黒|くろ}い{猫|ねこ}が{庭|にわ}を{歩|ある}いていた。
examples.english: A black cat was walking through the garden.

examples.japanese: うちの{猫|ねこ}は{人|ひと}が{好|す}きで、{誰|だれ}にでもすぐ{近|ちか}づいていく。
examples.english: Our cat loves people and goes right up to anyone.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{時|とき}に{拾|ひろ}った{猫|ねこ}をずっと{大切|たいせつ}にしていて、もう{十|じゅう}{年|ねん}も{一緒|いっしょ}に{暮|く}らしている。
examples.english: I've been taking good care of a cat I found as a child, and we've been living together for ten years now.

notes:
{猫|ねこ} means cat—the common domesticated feline.

TYPES OF CATS:
- {子猫|こねこ}: kitten
- {野良猫|のらねこ}: stray cat
- {飼|か}い{猫|ねこ}: pet cat
- {黒猫|くろねこ}: black cat
- {三毛猫|みけねこ}: calico cat

CAT-RELATED WORDS:
- {猫舌|ねこじた}: sensitive to hot food (lit. 'cat tongue')
- {猫背|ねこぜ}: hunched back, slouching
- {招|まね}き{猫|ねこ}: beckoning cat (lucky charm)

IDIOMS:
- {猫|ねこ}の{手|て}も{借|か}りたい: so busy I'd borrow even a cat's paws
- {猫|ねこ}をかぶる: to hide one's true nature (play innocent)
- {猫|ねこ}に{小判|こばん}: casting pearls before swine

CULTURAL NOTE:
Cats are popular in Japan—{猫カフェ|ねこカフェ} (cat cafés) are common, and cats appear often in anime and merchandise.
